_note: EASY -- the default, and the direct descendant of AIPlaytest.SCRIPT (PLAN.md 12.2a).
THE OPENING IS THE PROJECT OWNER'S OWN SCRIPT, RULE FOR RULE, in the order they
wrote it: two villagers to berries, one to stone, one to wood, the fifth starts a
house; the two drop-off camps beside the resources they serve; gold, then the age;
two more villagers, a mill and a field; then a house, a tower, a barracks and five
swordsmen. What changed is not the plan but what drives it -- every step used to
carry a TIMEOUT IN TICKS and was abandoned when it expired, which is how p2 gave up
on a barracks 73 wood short and died holding 950 (BUGS.md). A rule has no timeout.
It waits.
EVERY RULE CARRIES A CONDITION THAT GOES FALSE ONCE IT IS SATISFIED. Rules are
re-evaluated every think interval and the first match wins, so a rule that stayed
true would fire again and again -- five houses, five barracks. `fewer_than` counts
FOUNDATIONS and PRODUCTION QUEUES for exactly this reason: 'I have already started
one' has to read as 'I have one', or the AI orders another every half second while
the first is being built.
WHY THE OPENING GATHER RULES ARE CAPPED AT AGE 1. The standing orders (AISystem)
already put every idle villager on the poorest resource, which is a better rule
than any fixed split once the economy is running. These four exist to shape the
FIRST minute -- berries before wood, a stone gatherer before anybody needs stone --
and would otherwise fight the standing orders for the rest of the match.
DIFFICULTY, per AI_Player_difficulty.md: focus on building and defending; attacks
after 10 minutes of game time, then keeps going; ages to 2; one tower.
ARMY CAPS RISE WITH DIFFICULTY (project owner, 2026-08-27), and every one of them
is bounded by POPULATION rather than by taste. A unit is 1 pop, a town centre
gives 10 and a house 5, so the house count in each file has to carry the army the
same file asks for: Easy's 3 houses is a cap of 25 against 7 villagers and 10
swordsmen. Raise a cap without raising the houses and TrainCommand simply refuses
-- a bot that stops training for no visible reason.
THE 10-MINUTE TRIGGER IS A CLOCK, AND THAT IS NOT THE THING THE OWNER RULED OUT.
A per-step timeout ABANDONS A GOAL because the world was slower than a number
somebody guessed -- that is the defect. A global clock that decides when aggression
unlocks abandons nothing and does not depend on how far the gold is; it is a
handicap, deliberately expressed in time, and it is what makes Easy easy.
